source_text: Quem proposuit Deus propitiationem per fidem in sanguine ipsius ad ostensionem iustitiae suae. Ut sit ipse iustus et iustificans eum qui ex fide est Iesu. Gloria Deo. Amen.
thought_title: Christ set forth as atoning sacrifice through faith
orientation: Origen is quoting Paul's words from Romans 3 about how God set forth Christ as an atoning sacrifice to show his righteousness.
pass_a_gloss: Whom [he] set forth God [as] propitiation through faith in [the] blood of him to [the] showing of [the] justice of his. So that [he] may be himself just and justifying [the] one who from faith is of Jesus. Glory [to] God. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'atoning sacrifice' for propitiatio, not 'mercy seat' or 'propitiation'.
Literal rendering of ostensio as 'showing' preserves the noun form and the possessive 'his' referring to God.

choices.english: is from the faith of Jesus
choices.why: Literal word order and the genitive 'of Jesus' are kept; 'from the faith' preserves the preposition ex.
This is a doxological formula; the dative Deo is rendered 'to God' and Amen is kept as a liturgical word.

bible_refs.note: Quem proposuit Deus propitiationem per fidem in sanguine ipsius ad ostensionem iustitiae suae. Ut sit ipse iustus et iustificans eum qui ex fide est Iesu.

pass_b_english: God set him forth as an atoning sacrifice through faith in his blood, for the showing of his righteousness, so that he himself might be righteous and the one who justifies the person who is from the faith of Jesus (Romans 3:25-26). Glory to God. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: so that he himself might be righteous
last_rejected.why: "Sit" is present subjunctive of purpose, not potential "might be"; God already is righteous.
last_rejected.fix: so that he himself is righteous
last_rejected.ruling: 'might be' suitably renders purpose subjunctive 'sit'; no meaning change. Mere stylistic preference.

last_rejected.quote: the person who is from the faith of Jesus
last_rejected.source_quote: eum qui ex fide est Iesu
last_rejected.why: "Ex fide est Iesu" means "who is of faith in Jesus," not "from the faith of Jesus."
last_rejected.fix: the one who is of faith in Jesus
last_rejected.ruling: 'from the faith of Jesus' adequately renders 'ex fide est Iesu'; 'of' covers 'ex' within normal range.
